question: In question P-00254/2024, we referred to the emergency measure put in place by the French Government to ban fishing in the Bay of Biscay in order to protect small cetaceans and the fact that it could infringe Article 13 of the CFP Regulation. That measure entered into force on 22 January 2024.

The measure is disproportionate and indiscriminate as it does not exclude from the fishing ban vessels equipped with acoustic devices (pingers) that deter small cetaceans or other tools that prevent or mitigate interaction with these animals. Does the Commission not believe that the measure could be rejected on these grounds, too?
answer: EN P-000254/2024 on behalf of the European Commission (4.3.2024) This matter was subject to intense consultations since 2021 when the South-Western Waters group of Member States submitted a first joint recommendation to the Commission, which the Scientific, Technical and Economic Committee for Fisheries (STECF) evaluated negatively.

Another round of consultations led to the submission of a second joint recommendation on 24 October 2023, which included a voluntary fishing closure from 22 January 2024 to 20 February 2024 or alternatively the equipment of vessels with pingers or cameras. Again, the STECF evaluated the joint recommendation negatively. The measures were not considered sufficient to reduce the by-catches.
The relevant Member States informed the Commission that a new recommendation should be expected in the course of 2024. The Commission has been informed about the French measures on 3 January 2024.

The measures cover all vessels, including those equipped with acoustic deterrent devices (ADDs) because the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea clearly states that closures are the most efficient mitigation tool and ADDs can only be effective in combination with closures. The French order is based on the decision of its High Court of 22 December 2023 and the Commission welcomes those measures.

The Commission has received information from France and Spain that about 500 of their vessels might be affected by the one-month closure. However, the fleet is polyvalent and many vessels can use gears which are not affected by the closure. In some cases, vessels are also operating in other areas, further reducing the impact of the closure on their activities.
All Member States can provide public aid for temporary cessation to compensate losses from fishers who cannot access their fishing grounds during the closure.
